faqs.q: What are Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes used for?
faqs.a: Inhibited admiralty brass tubes (C44300, C44400, C44500; CuZn28Sn1As) to ASTM B111 and EN 12451, for condensers and coolers on clean fresh or brackish cooling water. It is listed in 7 sizes, 9.53–25.4 mm outside diameter.

faqs.q: How do I read an Indus part number for Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes, such as IH-TF-BR-ADM-0095-089?
faqs.a: Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes part numbers begin with IH-TF-BR-ADM and then give the outside diameter in tenths of a millimetre and the wall thickness in hundredths of a millimetre. IH-TF-BR-ADM-0095-089 is 9.53 mm outside diameter by 0.89 mm wall, and IH-TF-BR-ADM-0254-165 is the largest size listed. Quote the full part number, or the standard, grade, OD and wall.

faqs.q: What sizes do Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes come in?
faqs.a: Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes are listed in 7 sizes, 9.53–25.4 mm outside diameter, each with its own Indus part number, for example IH-TF-BR-ADM-0095-089 and IH-TF-BR-ADM-0254-165. The table includes 9.53 mm OD by 0.89 mm wall and 25.40 mm OD by 1.65 mm wall.

faqs.q: What do I need to send to order Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes to the right size and grade?
faqs.a: For Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes, quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the standard and grade, the outside diameter and wall (BWG or millimetres, minimum or average wall), the length and the quantity. We quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

faqs.q: What cooling-water velocity can Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes take?
faqs.a: The water velocity limit for Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes: ≈1.8 m/s; positioned for fresh and brackish cooling water. Where a figure is not listed for a size, we confirm it on the quotation.

faqs.q: Which materials and grades are Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes available in?
faqs.a: Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes are available in these grades: C44300 arsenical; C44400 antimonial; C44500 phosphorised; CW706R CuZn28Sn1As.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes?
faqs.a: Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes are made to ASTM B111, ASTM B395, ASTM B135, EN 12451, BS 2871 Pt 3, BS 2871, IS 1545, JIS H 3300, NES 779. Tell us the standard and grade on your enquiry; equivalent grades in other standards are indicative and are checked against each tender.

faqs.q: What do Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes connect to or fit with?
faqs.a: For Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes, condenser tubes are expanded into tube sheets and carried on support plates, and the tube metal must be matched to the tube sheet and water side to avoid galvanic problems. Related ranges are the [Copper Tubes](/c/copper-tubes) and [Copper Coils](/c/copper-coils) shelves.

faqs.q: How should Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes be inspected on receipt and stored?
faqs.a: Check Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes on receipt against the order: outside diameter, wall, length, marking and the certificate heat numbers, and keep the ends capped until installation. Handle and store the material so the surface is not scratched or dented.

faqs.q: How do Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes differ from Aluminium Brass Condenser Tubes?
faqs.a: Admiralty Brass Condenser Tubes differ from [Aluminium Brass Condenser Tubes](/p/aluminium-brass-condenser-tubes) in its base tube material C44300 arsenical; C44400 antimonial; C44500 phosphorised; CW706R CuZn28Sn1As against C68700; CW702R CuZn20Al2As. It also differs in its outside diameter 9.53–25.4 mm against 9.53–19.05 mm; wall thickness 0.89–1.65 mm against 0.91–1.22 mm.
